body.justification: This supporting theorem validates the atlas on the exact experimental overlap and on a fully specified selected assignment-boundary datum.
body.gap: Shingaki--Kuroki (2023), Theorem 1 and equations (8)--(11), identify and estimate the full response-type vector under no selection, randomized treatment, invertible cell matrices, and determinant-ratio separation; the cited theorem does not address selected forced-zero cycle fibers.
body.consumer: Experimental users can check agreement with the published plug-in estimand, while selected-data users can verify the separate boundary certificate under the present model.
body.proof_tex:
On the experimental submodel, \(S=1\) gives \(m=r\), and randomization gives \(P(U=i\mid X=x)=\pi_i\).  The cited 2023 theorem identifies the four response-type probabilities and makes its plug-in estimator consistent.  We now verify that its observable conditions also pin the larger cycle fiber, rather than merely the restricted experimental parameterization.

For a cell \(e=(x,y)\) and a proxy category \(w\), the determinant of the paper's \(2\)-by-\(2\) matrix \(Q_{xyw}\), after factoring out the positive cell probability twice, is
\[
\det\begin{pmatrix}
1&P(W=w\mid E=e)\\
P(Z=z_1\mid E=e)&P(W=w,Z=z_1\mid E=e)
\end{pmatrix}.
\]
For any two-component cycle factorization of that cell, direct expansion gives
\[
\det(Q_{xyw})=K_e\{b_i(w)-b_j(w)\}, \tag{1}
\]
where \(K_e\ne0\) does not depend on \(w\); nonvanishing follows from Condition (3).  Hence the determinant ratios in the paper are observable direction ratios for the affine line \(\mathcal L_e\).  The four inequalities in Condition (3) say exactly that the two incident directions used in each of equations (8)--(11) are distinct.  Those displayed equations are nonsingular two-by-two linear systems for the corresponding coordinates of the common endpoint.  Thus every \(T_e\) has rank two and, for each response type \(i\), its two incident observable lines meet in the unique point \(b_i\) recovered by those equations.

Apply the rank-two orientation theorem.  On every nonempty orientation chart, every endpoint interval is the singleton consisting of that incident-line intersection.  Therefore the whole \(\mathcal C_A(T)\) has one endpoint tuple and one coefficient tuple, and its target agrees with the generating experimental SCM.  In the paper's ordering, types \((00,01,10,11)\) correspond to the present types \((4,2,3,1)\), so
\[
\pi^{\mathrm{SK}}=(\pi_4,\pi_2,\pi_3,\pi_1).
\]
Response consistency and randomization then give
\[
\mathrm{PN}
=\frac{\pi_2}{\pi_1+\pi_2}
=\frac{\pi^{\mathrm{SK}}_2}{\pi^{\mathrm{SK}}_2+\pi^{\mathrm{SK}}_4},
\qquad
\mathrm{PS}
=\frac{\pi_2}{\pi_2+\pi_4}
=\frac{\pi^{\mathrm{SK}}_2}{\pi^{\mathrm{SK}}_1+\pi^{\mathrm{SK}}_2}.
\]
The positive observed cells make both denominators positive.  This proves
\(\mathcal T_A(p,r)=\{\phi_{\mathrm{SK}}(\pi^{\mathrm{SK}})\}\).  The all-rank-two branch is one of the oriented charts in the definition of \(\mathscr A\), so it returns this value.  By the cited plug-in consistency and continuity of \(\phi_{\mathrm{SK}}\) at positive denominators,
\[
\phi_{\mathrm{SK}}(\widehat\pi_n^{\mathrm{SK}})
\xrightarrow{P}\phi_{\mathrm{SK}}(\pi^{\mathrm{SK}}).
\]

We next check the boundary datum directly.  Each listed \(b_i^{\mathrm{bd}}\) is strictly positive and normalized.  In every cell, the two coefficient rows are nonnegative, have columnwise sum \(v_e=(1/3,1/3,1/3)\), and are not proportional.  The two incident endpoint columns are distinct, so
\[
\operatorname{rank}(T_e^{\mathrm{bd}})=2.
\]
At every \((w,z)\), at least one coefficient is positive and every endpoint coordinate is positive; hence every entry of \(T_e^{\mathrm{bd}}\), and therefore of \(p^{\mathrm{bd}}\), is positive.  Moreover
\[
\sum_es_e^{\mathrm{bd}}m_e^{\mathrm{bd}}
=\frac14\left(\frac18+\frac14+\frac38+\frac12\right)
=\frac5{16},
\]
and cell by cell
\[
\frac{s_e^{\mathrm{bd}}m_e^{\mathrm{bd}}}{5/16}=r_e^{\mathrm{bd}}.
\]
The cycle lift therefore gives \(\mathcal F_A(p^{\mathrm{bd}},m^{\mathrm{bd}})\ne\varnothing\).

In simplex coordinates, the relevant lines are
\[
\mathcal L_{11}=\mathcal L_{00}=\{b:b(w_2)=1/5\},
\quad
\mathcal L_{01}=\{b:b(w_1)=1/5\},
\quad
\mathcal L_{10}=\{b:b(w_3)=1/5\}.
\]
Thus the transverse intersections pin \(b_1^{\mathrm{bd}},b_3^{\mathrm{bd}},b_4^{\mathrm{bd}}\).  In cell \(11\), the normalized columns at \(z_1,z_3\) are respectively \(b_1^{\mathrm{bd}},b_2^{\mathrm{bd}}\), so the segment condition forces the type-\(2\) endpoint to lie at or beyond \(b_2^{\mathrm{bd}}\) away from \(b_1^{\mathrm{bd}}\).  In cell \(00\), those columns are \(b_2^{\mathrm{bd}},b_4^{\mathrm{bd}}\), so the same endpoint must lie at or beyond \(b_2^{\mathrm{bd}}\) away from \(b_4^{\mathrm{bd}}\).  The two closed half-line constraints meet only at \(b_2^{\mathrm{bd}}\).  All four endpoints, and hence all rank-two coefficients, are therefore fixed.  In particular the four displayed zero coefficients are compulsory, and
\[
\tau_C
=\left(0+\frac16+\frac13,\frac13+\frac16+0\right)
=\left(\frac12,\frac12\right).
\]
The rank-two theorem and the cycle lift prove the asserted singleton full-SCM target set.

The same argument is stable relative to the support face that retains the four indicated zero positions: the zero columns continue to expose the common endpoint, the strict endpoint order and the two transverse intersections remain strict conditions, and all other displayed probabilities remain positive.  These are relatively open inequalities, and the displayed datum is a member, so that chart is nonempty and rigid.  Finally \(r^{\mathrm{bd}}\ne m^{\mathrm{bd}}\), whereas \(S=1\) almost surely would imply \(r=m\); hence this datum is outside the no-selection experimental submodel.
